title: Hairy Cell Leukemia
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2027)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2027 clinical navigator for Hairy Cell Leukemia (Classic HCL and HCL-variant). Implements Workup First diagnostic checklists (bone marrow reticulin stain for dry tap, Annexin A1 / TRAP IHC, flow CD11c/CD25/CD103/CD123, mandatory BRAF V600E mutation testing), treatment indications vs watch-and-wait, frontline purine analogues (Cladribine / Pentostatin Category 1), and relapsed/refractory targeted therapies (Cladribine + Rituximab, Vemurafenib +/- Rituximab, Dabrafenib + Trametinib, Moxetumomab pasudotox). References StewardMD ONCQIS Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Hairy Cell Leukemia Version 1.2027 (July 24, 2026).

a.text: BRAF V600E mutation is present in more than 95% of classic HCL cases when tested by sensitive allele-specific PCR or next-generation sequencing, and is absent in HCL-variant and in most morphologic mimics such as splenic marginal zone lymphoma. Mandatory testing distinguishes classic HCL from HCL-variant and confirms eligibility for BRAF-directed therapy at relapse.

b.text: Annexin A1 immunohistochemistry is highly specific for classic hairy cell leukemia: it is positive in classic HCL and negative in HCL-variant, splenic marginal zone lymphoma, and other small B-cell lymphomas. TRAP (tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase) and Cyclin D1 are supportive but less specific. Bone marrow is frequently a dry tap because of marked reticulin fibrosis, so trephine biopsy with reticulin stain is required.

c.text: Treatment is indicated for symptomatic active disease: ANC below 1,000/mcL, hemoglobin below 10 g/dL, platelets below 100,000/mcL, symptomatic or progressive splenomegaly, recurrent or serious infections, or systemic B-symptoms. Asymptomatic patients with preserved counts are observed, since early treatment of indolent disease has not shown a survival advantage.

d.text: Purine nucleoside analogues cause profound and prolonged CD4 T-cell depletion. Mandatory Pneumocystis jirovecii prophylaxis (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) and varicella-zoster prophylaxis (acyclovir or valacyclovir) are required during and after therapy until CD4 recovery above 200/mcL. Screen for active or latent infection (including hepatitis B and C, tuberculosis, fungal and atypical mycobacterial infection) before starting therapy.

e.text: For early relapse or purine-refractory classic HCL, options include cladribine plus rituximab (375 mg/m2 weekly for 8 doses), BRAF-directed therapy (vemurafenib with or without rituximab, or dabrafenib plus trametinib), and moxetumomab pasudotox (anti-CD22 recombinant immunotoxin). Late relapse beyond 3 to 5 years may be retreated with the same purine analogue with or without rituximab.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: HCL: clinical presentation
nodes.description: Step 1: Clinical Presentation. Select the confirmed diagnosis and treatment history.
bullets: Classic hairy cell leukemia, newly diagnosed (BRAF V600E positive in more than 95% of cases)
Hairy cell leukemia-variant (HCL-v): BRAF V600E negative, CD25 negative, less responsive to single-agent purine analogues
Classic HCL, previously treated, now relapsed or refractory

options.label: Relapsed or refractory classic HCL (previously treated)

nodes.name: Classic HCL workup
nodes.title: Classic HCL: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Confirm classic HCL and establish baseline disease burden and infection risk. Complete every item before triaging to watch-and-wait versus treatment.
bullets: History and physical examination: spleen palpation for splenomegaly, lymph node survey, B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), performance status, prior infections and transfusion history
CBC with differential and comprehensive metabolic panel, LDH, renal and hepatic function; document ANC, hemoglobin, and platelet count against treatment thresholds
Peripheral blood smear examination: mature B-lymphocytes with circumferential hairy cytoplasmic projections; monocytopenia is a classic hallmark
Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy: dry tap is common because of marked reticulin fibrosis, so obtain trephine core with reticulin stain; classic fried-egg appearance with widely spaced nuclei
Bone marrow immunohistochemistry panel: CD20, Annexin A1 (highly specific for classic HCL), TRAP, CD25, Cyclin D1
Multiparameter flow cytometry on blood or marrow: co-expression of mature B-cell markers with bright CD11c, CD25, CD103, and CD123
Mandatory molecular testing: BRAF V600E mutation testing by allele-specific PCR or NGS (present in more than 95% of classic HCL; absent in HCL-variant)
Spleen and nodal assessment: contrast CT of abdomen and pelvis to quantify splenomegaly and internal lymphadenopathy

Infection workup before purine analogue therapy: screen for active or latent infections including fungal, atypical mycobacterial, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C disease; plan antimicrobial prophylaxis (Bactrim plus Acyclovir) with purine analogues

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed - Proceed to Treatment Indications

nodes.name: HCL-variant workup
nodes.title: HCL-variant: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Confirm HCL-variant and distinguish it from classic HCL and splenic marginal zone lymphoma. Complete every item before selecting frontline therapy.
bullets: History and physical examination: spleen palpation (often marked splenomegaly without the monocytopenia of classic HCL), lymph node survey, B-symptoms, performance status
CBC with differential and peripheral smear: hairy-appearing lymphocytes often with prominent nucleoli and higher leukocyte counts than classic HCL; typically no monocytopenia

Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy with reticulin stain: hypercellular marrow with interstitial infiltrate; IHC panel including CD20, Annexin A1 (negative in HCL-v), TRAP (often negative or weak), Cyclin D1
Multiparameter flow cytometry: bright CD11c and CD103 positive, but CD25 negative and CD123 negative or dim; CD200 typically negative, distinguishing HCL-v from classic HCL

Mandatory molecular testing: BRAF V600E testing by allele-specific PCR or NGS is negative in HCL-v; assess MAP2K1 mutation and TP53 deletion or mutation, which are enriched in HCL-v and inform prognosis
Exclude mimics: splenic marginal zone lymphoma and splenic diffuse red pulp lymphoma (Annexin A1 negative, CD103 variable); confirm diagnosis with combined morphology, immunophenotype, and genetics
Contrast CT of abdomen and pelvis to quantify splenomegaly and internal lymphadenopathy

Infection workup: screening for active or latent infections (fungal, atypical mycobacteria, HBV, HCV); antimicrobial prophylaxis (Bactrim plus Acyclovir) required if a purine analogue backbone is used

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed - Proceed to Treatment Indications

nodes.name: Treatment indications
nodes.title: Classic HCL: indications for therapy
nodes.description: Decide between watch-and-wait and active treatment using NCCN treatment-indication criteria.
bullets: Asymptomatic disease with preserved counts: observe without therapy
Symptomatic active disease meeting any threshold: ANC below 1,000/mcL, hemoglobin below 10 g/dL, or platelets below 100,000/mcL
Symptomatic or progressive splenomegaly, recurrent or serious infections, or systemic B-symptoms

options.label: Asymptomatic: normal counts or mild cytopenias without symptoms
Symptomatic active disease: cytopenias, splenomegaly, infections, or B-symptoms

nodes.name: Watch-and-wait
nodes.title: Active surveillance (watch-and-wait)
nodes.description: Observation for asymptomatic classic HCL until a treatment indication develops.
bullets: Routine CBC with differential and physical examination (spleen check) every 3 to 6 months

Reassess for treatment indications at each visit: ANC below 1,000/mcL, hemoglobin below 10 g/dL, platelets below 100,000/mcL, symptomatic or progressive splenomegaly, recurrent infections, or B-symptoms
No routine CT imaging in asymptomatic patients; image new or progressive symptoms
Counsel on infection vigilance given neutropenia and monocytopenia; vaccinate per immunocompromised-host guidance and avoid live vaccines during later purine analogue therapy
Begin purine analogue therapy when active-disease criteria are met

nodes.name: First-line therapy
nodes.title: Classic HCL: first-line purine analogue
nodes.description: Select the preferred Category 1 frontline purine nucleoside analogue.
bullets: Purine nucleoside analogues are the Category 1 preferred frontline therapy for symptomatic classic HCL
Cladribine suits patients who can receive a 5 to 7 day course with prompt count recovery planning
Pentostatin suits patients needing a dose-adjustable every-2-week schedule with renal-function monitoring
Both options require mandatory PJP and VZV prophylaxis until CD4 recovery above 200/mcL

nodes.name: Cladribine frontline
nodes.title: Frontline cladribine (Category 1 preferred)
nodes.description: Single-course cladribine for symptomatic classic HCL with mandatory infection prophylaxis.
bullets: Cladribine 0.09 to 0.14 mg/kg/day by continuous IV infusion for 7 days, OR 0.1 mg/kg/day as a 2-hour IV infusion for 5 days; approximately 85% complete remission rate
Single course is standard; assess response with CBC, marrow evaluation, and spleen reassessment, allowing several months for full count recovery before declaring failure
Mandatory PJP prophylaxis (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) and VZV prophylaxis (acyclovir or valacyclovir) during and after therapy until CD4 count recovers above 200/mcL
Monitor for prolonged myelosuppression, febrile neutropenia, and opportunistic infection; give growth-factor and transfusion support per thresholds
Avoid live vaccines during therapy and until immune reconstitution; counsel on fertility and secondary malignancy risk

nodes.name: Pentostatin frontline
nodes.title: Frontline pentostatin (Category 1 preferred)
nodes.description: Intermittent pentostatin for symptomatic classic HCL with renal monitoring and mandatory infection prophylaxis.
bullets: Pentostatin 4 mg/m2 IV every 2 weeks until maximum response plus 2 consolidation doses; hold or dose-reduce for renal dysfunction and monitor creatinine before each dose
Hydrate before and after each infusion; assess response with CBC, marrow evaluation, and spleen reassessment
Mandatory PJP prophylaxis (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) and VZV prophylaxis (acyclovir or valacyclovir) during and after therapy until CD4 count recovers above 200/mcL
Monitor for prolonged myelosuppression, nausea, rash, and opportunistic infection; avoid concurrent nephrotoxins
Avoid live vaccines during therapy and until immune reconstitution; counsel on fertility and secondary malignancy risk

nodes.name: Relapse timing
nodes.title: Relapsed or refractory HCL: relapse timing
nodes.description: Stratify relapsed or refractory classic HCL by time to relapse and prior purine analogue response.
bullets: Late relapse more than 3 to 5 years after first purine analogue: retreatment with the same agent remains effective
Early relapse within 2 to 3 years, or disease refractory to a purine analogue: switch to a rituximab combination, BRAF-directed therapy, or moxetumomab pasudotox
Re-biopsy and repeat BRAF V600E testing at relapse to confirm diagnosis and targeted-therapy eligibility

options.label: Late relapse: more than 3 to 5 years after prior purine analogue
Early relapse (under 2 to 3 years) or refractory to purine analogue

nodes.name: Retreat late relapse
nodes.title: Late relapse: retreat with same purine analogue +/- rituximab
nodes.description: Retreatment for classic HCL relapsing more than 3 to 5 years after first purine analogue.
bullets: Retreat with the same purine nucleoside analogue (cladribine or pentostatin) at standard frontline dosing
Add rituximab for deeper response in fit patients: 375 mg/m2 weekly for 8 doses starting with or after the purine analogue
Mandatory PJP prophylaxis (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) and VZV prophylaxis (acyclovir or valacyclovir) until CD4 count recovers above 200/mcL
Reassess marrow response and BRAF V600E status; if response is brief, move to the early-relapse pathway (cladribine plus rituximab, BRAF-directed therapy, or moxetumomab pasudotox)

nodes.name: Early relapse options
nodes.title: Early relapse or refractory: salvage options
nodes.description: Select salvage therapy for early relapse or purine-refractory classic HCL.
bullets: Cladribine plus rituximab for chemoimmunotherapy-eligible patients
BRAF V600E targeted therapy (vemurafenib with or without rituximab, or dabrafenib plus trametinib, Category 2A) for BRAF-mutated disease
Moxetumomab pasudotox (anti-CD22 recombinant immunotoxin) for purine-refractory disease
Confirm BRAF V600E status and infection screen before targeted or immunotoxin therapy

options.label: BRAF-directed therapy (Vemurafenib +/- Rituximab, or Dabrafenib + Trametinib)

nodes.name: Cladribine rituximab
nodes.title: Salvage cladribine + rituximab
nodes.description: Chemoimmunotherapy for early relapse or purine-refractory classic HCL.
bullets: Cladribine at standard dosing (0.1 mg/kg/day 2-hour IV infusion for 5 days or 7-day continuous infusion schedule) plus rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 8 doses
High complete remission and MRD-negative rates reported in relapsed classic HCL, including purine-refractory cases
Mandatory PJP prophylaxis (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) and VZV prophylaxis (acyclovir or valacyclovir) until CD4 count recovers above 200/mcL
Screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before rituximab and monitor for infusion reactions, prolonged cytopenias, and infection

nodes.name: BRAF directed therapy
nodes.title: Salvage BRAF-directed therapy (Category 2A)
nodes.description: BRAF inhibitor based therapy for BRAF V600E mutated early-relapse or refractory classic HCL.
bullets: Confirm BRAF V600E mutation by allele-specific PCR or NGS before starting BRAF-directed therapy
Vemurafenib 240 to 960 mg orally twice daily, with or without rituximab 375 mg/m2; combination with rituximab deepens and prolongs response
Alternative: dabrafenib plus trametinib (Category 2A), particularly when MEK co-inhibition is preferred for tolerance or resistance planning
Monitor for cutaneous toxicity (rash, photosensitivity, squamous proliferations), arthralgia, QT prolongation, pyrexia (dabrafenib plus trametinib), and ocular events; dose-modify per toxicity
Reassess blood counts, spleen size, marrow infiltration, and BRAF allele burden on therapy

nodes.name: Moxetumomab
nodes.title: Salvage moxetumomab pasudotox
nodes.description: Anti-CD22 recombinant immunotoxin for purine-refractory classic HCL.
bullets: Moxetumomab pasudotox (anti-CD22 recombinant immunotoxin) for classic HCL after at least two prior systemic therapies including a purine analogue, or for purine-refractory disease
Durable complete remissions including MRD-negative responses reported without further purine analogue exposure

Monitor specifically for capillary leak syndrome and hemolytic uremic syndrome: track weight, blood pressure, albumin, creatinine, LDH, platelets, and schistocytes; maintain hydration and hold therapy for grade 2 or higher toxicity
Premedicate and monitor infusions; assess marrow and MRD response after completed cycles
No PJP or VZV prophylaxis requirement intrinsic to the immunotoxin, but continue prophylaxis if CD4 depletion persists from prior purine analogues

nodes.name: HCL-v frontline
nodes.title: HCL-variant: frontline therapy
nodes.description: Select frontline therapy for HCL-variant, which responds poorly to single-agent purine analogues.
bullets: HCL-v lacks BRAF V600E and CD25 and is less responsive to single-agent cladribine or pentostatin, so combination or BTK-inhibitor therapy is preferred
Cladribine plus rituximab is the preferred frontline for fit patients with a treatment indication
Ibrutinib is the preferred option for patients unfit for purine analogue based chemoimmunotherapy
Relapsed HCL-v after prior therapy routes to the early-relapse salvage pathway

nodes.name: HCL-v cladribine rituximab
nodes.title: HCL-v frontline: cladribine + rituximab (preferred)
nodes.description: Preferred frontline chemoimmunotherapy for HCL-variant with a treatment indication.
bullets: Cladribine at standard dosing plus rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 8 doses; concurrent administration yields higher complete remission rates than sequential single-agent purine therapy in HCL-v
Single-agent purine analogues alone are discouraged in HCL-v because response rates and durability are inferior
Mandatory PJP prophylaxis (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) and VZV prophylaxis (acyclovir or valacyclovir) during and after the purine backbone until CD4 count recovers above 200/mcL
Screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before rituximab; monitor for infusion reactions, prolonged cytopenias, and infection
Assess response with CBC, marrow evaluation including Annexin A1 and TRAP IHC, and spleen reassessment

nodes.name: HCL-v ibrutinib
nodes.title: HCL-v frontline: ibrutinib (purine-unfit)
nodes.description: BTK-inhibitor frontline option for HCL-variant patients unfit for purine analogue therapy.
bullets: Ibrutinib continuous oral therapy for HCL-v patients unfit for purine analogue based chemoimmunotherapy or with TP53 aberration
Responses occur without the profound T-cell depletion of purine analogues, so no routine PJP or VZV prophylaxis is required
Monitor for bleeding risk (hold peri-procedure), atrial fibrillation and hypertension, diarrhea, arthralgia, and drug interactions via CYP3A
Assess response with CBC, spleen reassessment, and marrow evaluation; continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity
At progression, route to the early-relapse salvage pathway and consider clinical trial enrollment
